name: SysRepair-Bench
description: SysRepair-Bench is a reproducible benchmark of 313 Dockerized and virtual-machine scenarios for evaluating autonomous agents on real-world system-administration vulnerability remediation. Each scenario bundles (a) a launcher (Dockerfile or Vagrantfile) that boots a vulnerable target, (b) a natural-language threat description (threat.md or task.md.tmpl) covering severity, CVE/CWE references, affected service, and remediation hints, and (c) a verifier (verify.sh / verify.ps1 / verify-poc.sh / verify-service.ps1) that programmatically scores both vulnerability neutralization and service availability after the agent acts. The dataset is organized into suites (meta2, meta3-ubuntu, meta3-windows, meta4, meta4-ad-vm, ccdc, vulnhub, hivestorm) covering Linux containers, Windows containers, and Vagrant-managed Linux / Windows VMs.
citeAs: @inproceedings{sysrepairbench2026, title = {SysRepair-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents' Ability to Remediate Real-World System Vulnerabilities}, author = {Anonymous Authors}, booktitle = {NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (under review)}, year = {2026}, url = {https://anonymous.4open.science/r/sysrepair-bench-425F/}, note = {Double-blind submission #789}}
rai:dataCollection: All 313 scenarios were hand-authored by the SysRepair-Bench authors based on publicly disclosed Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) records, Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) categories, and public vendor advisories. For each target vulnerability the authors wrote (a) a launcher (Dockerfile or Vagrantfile) that boots a deliberately vulnerable target, (b) an English threat description (threat.md or task.md.tmpl) referencing the public CVE/CWE identifiers and citing the corresponding vendor or NVD documentation, and (c) a verifier script (verify.sh / verify.ps1 / verify-poc.sh / verify-service.ps1) that programmatically checks both vulnerability neutralization and continued service availability after agent action. No third-party machine-learning datasets were ingested. No human-subjects data was collected at any stage.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual authoring from public security disclosures
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Inputs to authoring were public artifacts only: NVD CVE entries, vendor security advisories (e.g., Apache, Atlassian, Microsoft, RedHat), MITRE CWE definitions, and openly-distributed vulnerable images (Metasploitable 2, Metasploitable 3, selected VulnHub images). All such inputs are linked or cited from the per-scenario threat document.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: None. The dataset is complete by construction: every scenario directory contains the launcher, threat document, and verifier required to score it. The manifest (scenarios.jsonl) records nullable fields (severity, CVSS, CVE list) as JSON null when the authoring threat document did not include the corresponding field; this is data absent from the source authoring, not missing collected data.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each scenario was authored and reviewed by the project authors. The 'annotation' for each scenario is the threat description plus the verifier script, both produced by the authors against the public CVE/CWE record being modeled. No external annotation workforce was used. No subjective labels were collected.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Authoring was performed locally in Git-tracked working trees; no third-party annotation platform was involved.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-author consistency was enforced by (a) a shared scenario template (launcher + threat.md + verify.sh/ps1), (b) requirement that each verifier pass on a known-vulnerable build before the scenario is accepted, and (c) requirement that each verifier reject a known-good (remediated) build. Disagreement on remediation strategy is resolved by treating any patch or compensating control that passes the verifier as a valid solution.
rai:dataAnnotatorDemographics: Not applicable. Annotations were produced by the authors only; no external annotator workforce was involved.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: None. All scenario authoring, threat descriptions, and verifier scripts were produced by human authors. Large-language-model output was used only as a writing aid for English-language editing of the threat documents (grammar, clarity) and never for generating verifier logic, exploit payloads, or remediation ground truth.
rai:dataPreprocessingImpactsOnDataQualit: None. Scenario records in scenarios.jsonl are emitted by a deterministic, lossless extractor (scripts/build_croissant_manifest.py) that copies fields verbatim from the authored sources. No filtering, balancing, or augmentation is applied.
rai:dataPreprocessingImpactsOnDataLabels: Not applicable. Ground-truth signals are produced at evaluation time by per-scenario verifier scripts, not by static labels.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (1) evaluating autonomous agent systems on real-world vulnerability remediation, (2) measuring the trade-off between vulnerability neutralization and preserved service availability, (3) studying agent reasoning about compensating controls when source patching is constrained, (4) ablating agent solver strategies (ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Solve, LATS) and the value of report-informed vs. zero-day variants, and (5) detecting regressions in agent system administration capability over time. Explicitly out-of-scope uses: training systems to generate novel zero-day exploits, weaponizing the included payloads against systems the user does not own or have written authorization to test, and any production deployment of un-remediated scenarios outside an isolated lab.
rai:dataBiases: The scenario corpus is biased toward Linux operating systems (approximately 80% of scenarios target Linux containers or Linux VMs; ~20% target Windows). Coverage is biased toward CVEs disclosed between 2010 and 2026 with public proof-of-concept availability — silently-patched or vendor-private vulnerabilities are under-represented. Threat documents are English-only. Severity skews toward High and Critical because those are the disclosures that motivated authoring. The hivestorm suite emphasizes free-roam hardening rather than single-CVE remediation, so single-CVE-trained agents may under-perform there.
rai:dataLimitations: Verifiers are heuristic: they check vulnerability exploitability via a representative proof-of-concept and service availability via a representative health probe, not exhaustive reachability. Agents may pass a verifier without addressing every variant of a vulnerability class. Scenarios marked as 'compensating-control eligible' (39 of 313) accept mitigations (network isolation, privilege restriction) that the underlying CVE record would not consider a true fix. Host-kernel-coupled scenarios (selected meta4 entries; meta4-ad-vm; hivestorm/scenario-13-ad-dc-win2019) require a vulnerable host kernel or Vagrant-managed VM and cannot be reproduced inside arbitrary cloud containers. Some scenarios are intentionally excluded from the official baseline run sets (see inspect_eval/runs.yaml) where the environment dependency is too strict.
rai:dataSocialImpact: All scenarios depict already-publicly-disclosed vulnerabilities; the dataset adds no new offensive capability that is not already documented in the corresponding public CVE records. The intended impact is defensive: enabling more rigorous evaluation of agent systems that remediate, harden, and respond to incidents on behalf of system administrators. The authors acknowledge the dual-use nature of any security research artifact: an agent trained or evaluated on remediation tasks could in principle be repurposed for offensive workflows. Mitigations: (a) the dataset does not include novel zero-day vulnerabilities; (b) all exploit payloads are minimal proof-of-concepts at the level already published in vendor advisories; (c) scenarios are designed to be run in isolated sandboxes, not against live infrastructure; (d) the CC-BY-4.0 license requires attribution but does not authorize unlawful use, and applicable computer-misuse laws continue to apply.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains no personally identifiable information (PII), no protected health information (PHI), no financial records, and no human-subjects data. Any usernames, hostnames, or IP addresses present in scenario fixtures are synthetic placeholders (e.g., admin / 127.0.0.1 / example.local).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Best-effort maintenance with no service-level agreement. Versioned releases are tagged in the source repository; bug reports and remediation-strategy corrections are accepted via the repository's issue tracker. During the NeurIPS 2026 double-blind review window the dataset is mirrored at the anonymized URL only; upon acceptance, the de-anonymized canonical URL and contact channel will replace the anonymous mirror. No commitment is made to backport fixes to prior tagged releases.

distribution.name: scenarios.jsonl
distribution.description: Per-scenario manifest: one JSON object per scenario describing suite, path, kind (linux-container | windows-container | vagrant-vm), launcher file, verifier file, threat document, and extracted CVE/CWE/severity/CVSS metadata. Records are sorted by scenario_id for deterministic ordering.

distribution.name: scenario-bundles
distribution.description: Per-scenario source bundles. Each scenario directory contains a launcher (Dockerfile or Vagrantfile), an English threat document (threat.md or task.md.tmpl), and a verifier script (verify.sh on Linux, verify.ps1 on Windows). Some scenarios include additional fixtures (entrypoints, seed scripts, sample exploit payloads).

distribution.name: inspect-eval-harness
distribution.description: Inspect AI-based evaluation harness, scorers, solvers, and run presets used to reproduce the paper's baselines (MiniMax-M2.7, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-9B with ReAct and ablation solvers).

distribution.name: openvas-scan-reports
distribution.description: OpenVAS scan reports used to seed the report-informed evaluation variant. PDF artifacts covering Metasploitable 2 and Metasploitable 3 (Ubuntu and Windows).

distribution.name: README
distribution.description: Top-level README with setup, suite descriptions, and reproduction instructions.

recordSet.name: scenarios
recordSet.description: One record per scenario across all eight suite directories. Records are extracted by scripts/build_croissant_manifest.py and emitted to scenarios.jsonl. Coverage: 313 scenarios (meta2: 40, meta3-ubuntu: 19, meta3-windows: 21, meta4: 117, meta4-ad-vm: 20, ccdc: 50, vulnhub: 30, hivestorm: 16).

field.name: scenario_id
field.description: Globally unique scenario identifier of the form '<suite>/<directory-name>', e.g. 'meta4/scenario-15' or 'hivestorm/scenario-13-ad-dc-win2019'.

field.name: suite
field.description: Scenario suite. One of: meta2, meta3-ubuntu, meta3-windows, meta4, meta4-ad-vm, ccdc, vulnhub, hivestorm.

field.name: path
field.description: Repository-relative path to the scenario directory (the FileSet entry containing the launcher, threat document, and verifier).

field.name: kind
field.description: Execution environment for the scenario. One of: linux-container, windows-container, vagrant-vm, windows-vm.

field.name: launch_file
field.description: Filename of the launcher inside the scenario directory. Typically 'Dockerfile' for container scenarios or 'Vagrantfile' for VM scenarios.

field.name: verify_file
field.description: Filename of the verifier script that programmatically scores remediation. 'verify.sh' for Linux scenarios, 'verify.ps1' for Windows scenarios, or 'verify-poc.sh' / 'verify-service.ps1' for VM scenarios that split the two checks across host and guest.

field.name: threat_file
field.description: Filename of the natural-language threat description shown to the agent (in the report-informed variant) and used as the ground-truth scope description. Typically 'threat.md' or 'task.md.tmpl'.

field.name: title
field.description: Title of the threat (first H1 heading in the threat document). May be null for free-roam hardening scenarios that do not have a single-vulnerability framing.

field.name: severity
field.description: Severity tier parsed from the threat document. One of: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational. Null for free-roam scenarios.

field.name: cvss
field.description: CVSS base score parsed from the threat document, if present.

field.name: cves
field.description: List of CVE identifiers referenced in the threat document. Empty for scenarios tracking pure configuration weaknesses.

field.name: cwes
field.description: List of CWE identifiers referenced in the threat document.
